correctness.rationale: Subtracting the vertex equations gives the stated symmetric edge generator, acting on precisely the zero-sum gradients. Transport of positive gradient entries to negative ones decomposes each gradient into signed two-coordinate dipoles with additive weighted norm. Thus it is exact to maximize over these dipoles, each realized by an arc indicator. One-sided expansion gives F_ij and the sharp initial rate; submultiplicativity via N_w(t/m)^m gives the exponential bound. For pairs at distance >=3 the column neighbor supports do not overlap and F_ij=(Mw)_i+(Mw)_j. The far graph is (n-5)-regular. At n=7 the step-three graph is an odd cycle, at n=8 steps of length three connect and the cited five-cycle is valid, and at n>=9 steps three and four connect and 0,3,6 is a triangle. Summing nonpositive far-pair tests forces equality at each edge; the odd cycle and connectivity force Mw=0, and the positive energy form makes w constant. Then column stochasticity proves contraction. At constant weights near-pair tests are strictly negative from direct communication or a shared neighbor. Thus sufficiently small nonconstant perturbations work for n<=5; for n=6 choose nonzero M u of alternating signs, possible by symmetry and the one-dimensional kernel, and the perturbation preserves the antipodal equalities. Checking the near-pair supports gives A_i and B_i in the stipulated uniform-mass regimes; on C_6 harmonicity of the opposite sums forces them equal, and the alternating-weight distance-two test gives |epsilon|<=1/3. Common mass scaling multiplies rates by a positive constant and leaves the test unchanged.
residual_risks: The finite script was inspected, not executed. Its explicit time-step check uses I+tM; actual small-time variation growth for the heat semigroup follows from the analytic expansion, not from an exact positive-time simulation.
The explicit A_i and B_i classification is for uniform masses; general positive masses have the F_ij tests and the rigidity/existence threshold.

value.rationale: The result decides whether edge variation weights can be independently designed to retain contraction under inhomogeneous holding rates. The sharp transition survives arbitrary masses even though the uniform-mass symmetry is lost, and the proof explains why the far-pair graph and its six-edge exception control it. The exact tests and arc witnesses let one check or falsify an individual design, not just infer failure asymptotically. This is useful beyond repeating the indexed uniform classification.
residual_risks: Specific to finite simple cycles with fixed positive variation weights and unit edge conductances; no general-graph statement is inferred.
